item.title: Rising temperatures are transforming Ireland into a rare wine country; the island now has 42 vineyards with upcoming bumper crops
item.description: As climate change enhances grape-growing conditions, Irish winemakers foresee a bountiful harvest. Expanding vineyards are drawing considerable attention from international investors. The unique interplay of soil and coastal weather is enabling the production of exquisite wines. To adapt to Ireland's cooler climate, new grape varieties are being introduced, with a focus on high-quality output to ensure competitiveness on the global stage.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why did Lacy cancel his stream with Mark Wahlberg? Here’s what happened
item.description: Streamer Lacy opted out of a collaboration with actor Mark Wahlberg due to his desire for a more authentic interaction rather than a superficial promotional appearance. Upon discovering Wahlberg's previous engagements with other creators, Lacy felt disheartened. He reiterated the importance of genuine connections, ultimately deciding that the collaboration's scripted nature did not align with his vision for a natural experience.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Deepwater Horizon damaged deep-sea corals in 2010; NOAA is now restoring them 16 years later
item.description: In a groundbreaking initiative, scientists are working to revive deep-sea coral ecosystems that were harmed by an oil spill. Utilizing corals grown in laboratories along with advanced tools, they have successfully deployed these corals at great depths. This project focuses on rejuvenating delicate habitats in the Gulf of Mexico, with ongoing monitoring set to evaluate both the survival rates of the corals and the overall restoration of the ecosystem.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Harry Potter fans forced a power cable between UK and Ireland to be relocated as it would desecrate the 'grave' of Dobby
item.description: In a heartwarming victory for Harry Potter fans, a significant power cable, originally set to cross Dobby the elf's cherished fictional grave, was successfully rerouted. The Greenlink interconnector project, valued in the multimillions, was adjusted to preserve this beloved memorial. Developers resorted to horizontal drilling to lay the cable underground, safeguarding Dobby's resting place on Freshwater West beach from any desecration.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Michigan to remove the Sanback Dam in 2026, restoring 14 wetland acres and protecting more than 70 downstream miles
item.description: The historic removal of a dam in Michigan, over a century old, is set to rejuvenate the region's natural ecosystems. This collaborative project will facilitate the movement of aquatic life by clearing upstream habitats while addressing the environmental threats posed by polluted sediments. Restoration efforts will focus on enhancing wetlands and safeguarding vital cold water habitats downstream, fostering biodiversity and ecological balance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Student Lillie Vehling rescued 3 girls drowning in Lake Washington during Blue Angels weekend
item.description: College student Lillie Vehling rescued three girls from Lake Washington during Seafair weekend. She noticed the girls struggling beyond the buoy line and immediately entered the water. Vehling, a former lifeguard and water polo player, brought the girls to safety one by one. First responders arrived and provided medical assistance after the successful rescue. Seafair honored Vehling as the "Lady Guardian of Lake Washington" for her bravery.

item.title: If vivid dreams leave you exhausted, experts say the problem may not be the dreams but disruptions that prevent deep sleep
item.description: Feeling fatigued after dreaming is often linked to disrupted sleep patterns, especially during REM phases. During REM, the brain remains highly engaged, which prevents achieving deeper rest. If dreams are recalled, it signals that you woke while dreaming, interrupting the crucial restorative stages of sleep. This interference obstructs clearing adenosine, a natural sleep-inducing byproduct, making tiredness arise from your awakening moment rather than the dreams themselves.

item.title: More than 99% of California’s sunflower sea stars vanished, now scientists have found a mysterious colony that could help revive dying kelp forests
item.description: Ten years ago, sunflower sea stars faced near extinction due to a devastating marine epidemic, leading to unchecked sea urchin populations that destroyed essential kelp forests. Recently, a newly identified colony of these sea stars has rekindled hope for ecological restoration. Researchers are examining their resilience to diseases, which could greatly benefit efforts to reintroduce these vital predators to their ocean habitats.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Minnesota church closes after 70 years, gives $600,000 to nonprofits and supports housing
item.description: St. Mark's United Church of Christ closed after seven decades due to declining membership. The congregation distributed approximately $600,000 among 21 local nonprofits. A substantial gift of $115,000 went to Loaves & Fishes for meal provision. The church property will be redeveloped into affordable housing units for the community. This act ensures the church's legacy continues through support and new homes.

item.title: Why Putin’s first Kuril Islands visit matters as Russia-Japan ties hit new low
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin visited the disputed Kuril Islands for the first time. This visit occurred amid deeply strained relations between Russia and Japan. Japan strongly protests the visit, reiterating its territorial claims over the islands. The long-standing dispute has intensified since Russia's invasion of Ukraine. This territorial disagreement prevents a formal World War II peace treaty.
